plan: For capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration limit.
This strategy prioritizes safety and reduces overall portfolio risk.
Maintain a significant cash buffer for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5% monthly return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged positions and maintaining a cash buffer.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to reduce overall leverage and meet the combined limit.
Reduce QQQI to 25% to comply with the single-name concentration rule.
Buy OXY at 4% as a new, high-scoring long setup from the scanner.
This plan balances growth potential with risk management, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5% monthly growth by blending broad index exposure with quality tech and limited leverage. It prioritizes risk management while seeking reasonable returns, with moderate drawdown potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name concentration limit.
Increase exposure to METU, MSFU, PLTU, SOXL, MUU, and SPAL, leaning into leveraged and uptrending tech.
Buy OXY at 6% as a new, high-scoring long setup from the scanner.
This plan uses leverage and concentration to target higher growth, with strict stop discipline.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly growth by leveraging high-scoring setups and increasing exposure to leveraged ETFs. Be aware this significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential; leveraged ETFs decay daily, and losses can be substantial without strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize steady monthly distributions.
This plan focuses on generating reliable income with minimal growth and low drawdown.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% monthly yield by rotating into income-focused ETFs and broad index funds. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable distributions, but remember distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
